svg.text: K11 The well: a slim dishwasher tub under the bench
The bench lifts on a front hinge, the hand hangs pots, boards and dishes in fork combs, the donor dishwasher washes and rinses at 82 °C.
final rinse ≥ 82 °C held 60 s on the coldest item → A0 ≈ 95
donor: 45 cm slim dishwasher ≈ €300 (pumps, heater, softener)
SIDE SECTION through the well column (X ≈ 3300)
A0 = Σ 10^((T − 80)/10) · Δt at the surface: ≈ 95 against the required 60 (margin 1.6 ×).
Heated by the donor’s own heater; rinse NTC; validated with loggers on a heavy pan and a PE board.
Household programmes for comparison: 65 °C 10 min → A0 19; 70 °C 10 min → 60.
ready for the next meal ≈ 25 min
Between meals the closed, dried well is the clean store for big ware and dishes.
Raw-meat jug and red items go to a turnaround load during the meal (same 82 °C rinse).
top view: bench over the mouth

g.text: 1/9 Bench cleared: the well lid (= bench) swings up on its front hinge; the hatch shows "busy".
2/9 The hand lowers a pan and hangs it by its stub in the upper fork comb (z 800).
3/9 A cutting board goes into the lower comb (z 700); the hand leaves upwards.
4/9 The insulated lid closes on its gasket: the tub is now a closed dishwasher.
6/9 Wash at 55–60 °C with detergent; the donor heater and pump are reused.
7/9 Final rinse ≥ 82 °C held 60 s on the coldest item: A0 ≈ 95, enough to disinfect.
8/9 Fan dry with the lid ajar; the vapour goes to the cell extraction.
9/9 Clean and dry: the closed well is the clean store until the next meal.
